source.title: The Complexity Dynamics of Grokking
source.authors: B. DeMoss; Silvia Sapora; J. Foerster; Nick Hawes; Ingmar Posner

record.tranche_reason: The paper says it reproduces a subset of the original modular-arithmetic grokking experiments and reports training and test accuracy during training.
record.gate_note: The text reports training and test accuracy in Figure A.10 and explicitly states that grokking occurs in all regularized models but not in unregularized models. Complexity and effective-rank trajectories are also reported; these measure the paper's proposed complexity account, not the circuit or progress-measure claims in V2. Values displayed only in figures are recorded as figure only. The paper does not report a training-set-size sweep.
record.test_reason: The paper reruns a subset of the Power et al. modular-arithmetic grokking tasks (p=113; +, ×, −, ÷) and reports train and test accuracy over training (Fig A.10). It states grokking occurs in all regularized models and in none of the unregularized ones. That bears directly on V1 in its original setting. The complexity and effective-rank tracking is the paper's own construct: the complexity fall coincides with the jump rather than anticipating it, and no circuit is identified, so it does not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors argue that a complexity phase transition is the central mechanism of grokking: complexity rises at memorization and falls at generalization in properly regularized nets, while unregularized nets stay at high complexity. They argue weight norm and linear structure are only partial proxies for complexity. They add that grokking is 'a sign of improperly regularized training'. They also claim their spectral-entropy regularizer causes grokking and gives lower-complexity models than weight decay.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it reproduces a subset of the original modular-arithmetic grokking experiments. It adds spectral-entropy and noise regularization and measures complexity through coarse-graining and compression; the text does not establish that all original training details are identical.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking differs between the regularized and unregularized training conditions. The four tasks use different training-data fractions: 20% for addition and multiplication, and 30% for subtraction and division.

fits_no_version.finding: Coarse-grained complexity rises during memorization and falls as regularized models generalize; unregularized models stay at high complexity. Effective rank falls at generalization under regularization and stays near full rank without it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In modular-arithmetic grokking, a compression-based complexity measure and effective rank peak at memorization and drop coincident with generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper's spectral-entropy regularizer yields lower complexity, smaller total description length and tighter (still vacuous) generalization bounds than weight decay alone or no regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral-entropy regularization produces more compressible grokked models than weight decay alone.

record.peer_reviewed: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
record.problems: Accuracy and trajectory values are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The paper reports mean curves over six seeds for the relevant figures but gives no numerical delay estimates. Training-set fraction is fixed by task, so the claim that smaller training sets require more optimization is not tested.

untested.parts: How the delay scales with training-set size: each task uses a single fixed train fraction (20% or 30%).
Not tested: no circuit identification, no measurement of memorizing-component removal, no test of whether a progress measure anticipates the jump.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich manipulation.
Not tested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Not tested: no critical dataset size, no ungrokking, and no circuit-efficiency analysis. The regularized-vs-unregularized contrast is consistent with V5 but does not isolate weight decay.
Not tested: no comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
Not tested: no optimizer-instability or softmax floating-point controls.

missing.what: Train and test accuracy trajectories for the weight-decay-only baseline. The text refers to 'weight decayed models' (Fig A.7) and to comparisons with 'weight decay alone'. Whether these models grok is needed to separate the effect of weight decay from the paper's regularizer.
missing.locator: Section 5; Fig A.7; Fig A.10; Fig A.11

missing.what: Approximate step at which the regularized models generalize (around 10^3 steps per the Fig A.9 caption), needed to size the delay.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Every accuracy result is figure-only. Seed counts differ across figures (3 in Fig 1, 6 in Figs 2 and A.10). The unregularized condition's optimizer settings are not described in the text. The regularized condition bundles three regularizers together (spectral entropy, noise, weight decay), so the V1 contrast cannot attribute grokking to any one of them.

versions.untested_parts: The dependence of the delay on training-set size is not tested; each task uses the stated fixed training-data fraction.

The paper tracks complexity and effective rank, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, measure formation/removal of circuit components, or test whether a progress measure anticipates the accuracy transition.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The paper compares its spectral-entropy regularizer with weight decay, but does not test the efficient-circuit account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
The paper does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The paper does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts as explanations of the delay.

relationships.condition: Regularized 1–2 layer transformers (spectral entropy + noise + AdamW wd=1) on mod-113 +, ×, −, ÷
relationships.reason: Train accuracy saturates quickly and test accuracy later jumps to perfect for all four tasks (A01, A02, A05, A06, A09, A10, A13, A14); values are figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated quickly, while test accuracy later jumped to perfect on addition, multiplication, subtraction, and division.

relationships.condition: Unregularized transformers on the same four tasks and train fractions
relationships.reason: The models memorize but never generalize within the training run (A03/A04, A07/A08, A11/A12, A15/A16), so the jump depends on regularization.
relationships.display_finding: Across the four tested tasks and training fractions, models memorized but never generalized within the training run.

reader_labels.condition: regularized modular-arithmetic models across the four tested operations
reader_labels.reason: The text reports rapid training-set memorization followed by grokking and perfect test accuracy for regularized models (A01, A02, A05, A06, A09, A10, A13, A14).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: unregularized modular-arithmetic models across the four tested operations
reader_labels.reason: The unregularized models memorize but do not generalize in the reported experiments (A03, A04, A07, A08, A11, A12, A15, A16); the result therefore depends on the training regime.
